q: Which exterior wall material best suits this facility's warehouse portion?
n: A predominantly concrete envelope gives the warehouse the durability, fire resistance, and low-maintenance mass appropriate for an industrial storage and production building, unlike glazed or largely steel-clad facades, which are less suited to that use and exposure.
scenario: A manufacturing firm plans to develop its 10,000-sqm rectangular interior lot in an industrial (I-2) district of Caloocan City. The parcel has an 80-meter frontage on its west side and drops at a 4% grade toward a 6-meter-wide creek along its eastern boundary. That west frontage faces a road used around the clock by container vans and trucks — a 30-meter-wide right-of-way that drains north at roughly a 1% cross-slope and carries 2.4-meter sidewalks on each side, with the sidewalk surface at the middle of the frontage set as elevation 0.0m. Two secondary streets, each on a 6.0-meter right-of-way, cross the primary road at right angles, and the two resulting corners are chamfered 6 meters with 4.25-meter legs. A private office building adjoins the property on one side and a ceramics plant on the other; across the main road sit two karaoke lounges and a resto-bar with live bands, while two-storey row houses stand on the far side of the creek. The owner wants a design that boosts profitability through efficient vertical and spatial organization and smooth workflow, applies sustainable design principles, and gives the area a recognizable architectural landmark.

q: Given the round-the-clock container van and truck traffic on this site, what minimum stall size should be allotted for parking an articulated truck?
n: An articulated (trailer-truck) vehicle needs a 3.60 m by 18.00 m stall as its minimum parking allowance, enough width and length to accommodate the tractor-trailer combination and allow safe maneuvering (Source: National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096), IRR Rule VII — parking slot standards for articulated/trailer trucks).

q: For a production area doing only bench and table assembly of small components, with no overhead ducts intruding, what ceiling height is needed?
n: For light bench/table assembly work with no overhead ductwork or crane clearance to accommodate, a 4.25 m ceiling height is sufficient for adequate ventilation and comfort without the added cost of the taller clearances needed for heavier industrial processes.

q: Where is the best location for the factory's first-aid station?
o: Away from the production floor so it doesn't interrupt workflow
Right at the factory's main entrance
As near the production floor as practicable
n: Placing first aid as close as possible to the production area minimizes response time for workplace injuries, which is where accidents are most likely to occur, rather than tucking it away in the admin wing or at the entrance where it's farther from the point of need.

q: For a large factory housing several distinct activities on one continuous open floor, which approach works best?
o: Wall off each activity individually with 150mm-thick CHB partitions, since open planning is discouraged
Assign each activity zone a floor color code and have workers wear uniforms matching their zone's color
Any of the above approaches would work equally well
Interweave the different activities throughout the floor instead of separating them, for flexibility
n: Color-coding the floor by activity zone and matching worker uniforms to that color scheme keeps the open floor plan intact for flexibility while still giving clear visual zoning, supervision, and safety demarcation — without the cost and rigidity of full masonry partitions.

q: On a factory building with very large bulk, which line type should dominate the street-facing elevation?
n: Emphasizing horizontal lines on a large industrial mass visually stretches and lowers the building's apparent bulk, breaking up the scale of the elevation so it reads as less massive and imposing from the street.

q: Which lighting fixture type best suits illuminating the factory floor?
n: Recessed troffer fixtures set into a suspended grid or ceiling deliver even, glare-controlled, high-output illumination suited to the uniform, task-oriented lighting levels factory floors need, while keeping fixtures clear of overhead crane paths, ducting, and material-handling equipment.

q: Along the creek bordering the site, what minimum easement must be observed?
n: Because the property sits within Caloocan City's urban area, the creek's bank is subject to the 3-meter minimum easement of public use set for urban areas — the 20-meter and 40-meter widths apply instead to agricultural and forest areas, respectively (Source: PD 1067 (Water Code of the Philippines), Article 51).

q: Given the site's I-2 industrial zoning, what is the maximum number of storeys allowed?
n: Under the density/height regulations applicable to I-2 (medium industrial) zoning, a building on this classification is generally capped at roughly 7 storeys, striking a balance between the zone's industrial bulk allowances and surrounding low-rise residential and commercial uses (Source: Locational/zoning height regulations for I-2 (Medium Industrial) districts, per NBC/HLURB zoning guidelines).
